title: How to work a quarter cross-stitch
subtitle: The smallest fractional stitch, for softening corners and curves
excerpt: A quarter cross-stitch is a single diagonal running from one corner of the Aida square to the centre hole. It pairs with a three-quarter cross-stitch to share a square, which is how rounded edges appear in a charted design.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive, fractional stitch chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: A half-diagonal stitch running from one corner of the Aida square to the centre hole. Always paired with a three-quarter cross-stitch from an adjacent corner to fill the same square.

The hole at the intersection of four Aida squares. The destination of fractional stitches (quarter and three-quarter), reached by passing the needle through the weave rather than a standard grid hole.

A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.

Angle the needle diagonally toward the centre of the square and push it through the Aida weave at the midpoint. The needle tip goes through the fabric threads, not through a grid hole.
Pull the floss through to the back, keeping the tension the same as for a full cross. The stitch should sit flat and reach cleanly to the midpoint.

Work the three-quarter cross-stitch in the same square (from the opposite corner, to the same centre hole, then back up to a third corner). The two stitches together fill the square with two colours or shades.

items.symptom: The stitch looks too short and doesn't reach the centre
items.cause: The needle is going into a grid hole rather than the centre of the weave block.
items.fix: Feel for the slight resistance at the middle of the Aida square. The needle tip should push through the fabric threads, not slide cleanly through a hole.

items.symptom: The fabric puckers around the centre point
items.cause: The stitch is being pulled too tight when the needle exits the weave.
items.fix: Use the same light tension as a full cross. Let the stitch sit at the same tension as its neighbours, not drawn tighter.

items.symptom: The two fractional stitches in the same square look uneven
items.cause: The quarter and three-quarter stitches were worked in different thread counts.
items.fix: Use the same strand count for both stitches in the shared square. Check the chart legend, which usually specifies two strands for full coverage and one strand for fractionals on fine fabric counts.

content.text: Quarter stitches rarely appear without their paired three-quarter companions on the same square. Once both fractional stitches feel natural, look for project tutorials with curved outlines. Those charts show alternating quarter and three-quarter symbols in a column or row.
